title: Docs site content staging and canary publishing playbook
author: Mariana Liu
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the recommended workflow, guardrails, and automation for staging content and performing canary releases on the Redwood Docs site. It targets engineering and Developer Experience (DX) contributors who publish SDK guides, API examples, quickstarts, and operational runbooks. The goal is to reduce regressions, enable fast rollbacks, and provide measurable confidence before a full live rollout.

Why a dedicated staging + canary process:
- Docs changes can break sample code or surface incorrect configuration; content bugs have measurable downstream developer and support cost.
- A controlled canary reduces blast radius while exercising real traffic patterns and external integrations (SDK downloads, snippet execution, embed previews).
- Automation ensures repeatable checks across authors and teams.

Scope and non-goals:
- Applies to: changes to SDK guides, API reference pages, quickstarts, code snippets, and example assets hosted in the docs repo.
- Does not cover: internal-only HR or legal documents, static marketing pages served from the marketing CDN (unless they reference SDK assets).

Owners and roles:
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience docs engineering (contact: @mariana.liu)
- Release engineer: rotates weekly from eng-platform (oncall: docs-release)
- Reviewer: content authors and at least one SDK owner for code-containing pages
- SRE: supports monitoring and rollback procedures

Key concepts and terminology:
- Staging site: ephemeral environment that mirrors production (same template, feature flags toggled off), used for pre-canary verification. URL: staging.docs.redwood.com
- Canary: a subset of live production traffic routed to a candidate content version (e.g., 5% of readers)
- Healthy canary: canary that meets all automated checks (see Acceptance criteria)

Acceptance criteria (must pass before increasing canary traffic):
1) CI passes: linting, link-check, snippet unit tests, spellcheck, and static type checks.
2) Live smoke tests: critical examples execute successfully against the staging backend (see smoke test suite).
3) Observability: no unexpected 5xx errors, no new client-side JS errors above threshold, and no increases in average page render time > 15%.
4) Manual review: at least one reviewer approves content with embedded code samples.

Process: staging -> canary -> rollout
1) Author creates a PR in docs repo targeting the main branch and includes the following checklist in the PR description:
   - Pages modified (list)
   - SDKs impacted (list)
   - Smoke test IDs to run
   - Rollback plan summary
2) CI runs automated checks and deploys the PR to the staging site on successful checks.
3) The author invites reviewers and resolves comments.
4) Once reviewers sign off, the release engineer initiates a canary deployment.

Canary deployment steps (engineer-run):
1) Tag the main deploy pipeline with a canary flag: 
   - CI job: docs-deploy-canary
   - Command: ./ci/run_deploy.sh --env=production --mode=canary --canary-weight=5
2) Route 5% of traffic using the routing layer (examples below).
3) Run the live smoke test suite against the canary cohort.
4) Monitor metrics for 30 minutes:
   - Page error rate (5xx) < 0.1%
   - Client JS exception rate change < 20% relative to baseline
   - Average render time change < 15%
   - Support ticket spike: none for pages in canary list
5) If checks pass, increment canary weight to 25% for 60 minutes, then 50% for 30 minutes; if stable, proceed to 100% and mark release complete.
6) If any check fails, immediately rollback:
   - Command: ./ci/run_deploy.sh --env=production --mode=rollback --target=previous-stable
   - Notify #docs-release and create a postmortem issue ticket with label docs-canary-failure

Smoke test suite (examples):
- SDK snippet runner: executes JavaScript, Python, and Go snippets in a sandbox against the staging inference API and verifies output shape and non-empty response.
- Embed preview test: validates OEmbed rendering for example notebooks and Gists.
- Download and checksum: verifies referenced SDK package tarballs match expected checksums in package-metadata.yml.
- Cross-browser render: headless Chrome run to assert no visual regressions for critical templates.

Routing examples:
- CDN edge rule: geo-aware header + cookie switch (for anonymous readers).
- A/B proxy config: local NGINX maps 5% of requests to canary backend pool.
- Feature-flag router: if user.hasFlag('docs_canary'), route to candidate version.

Rollbacks and emergency fixes:
1) Immediate rollback criteria: any of the canary acceptance checks fail, or high-severity security/PII exposure detected.
2) Rollback procedure:
   - Trigger rollback pipeline (see command above).
   - Reapply last-known-good content to staging and run full smoke suite.
   - Open incident in incident-dashboard, tag SRE and docs owner.
   - Draft a short customer-facing note if the change was public and likely noticed.

Post-release validation and telemetry:
- Release engineer posts a summary to #docs-release with the canary weights, duration, and any anomalies.
- Instrumentation to capture per-page canary IDs and sample user-agent for debugging.
- Run a 24-hour passive watch for the pages included in the canary cohort and escalate on unusual traffic or errors.

Developer guidance: snippet hygiene checklist:
- Keep snippets minimal and idempotent.
- Use the canonical SDK client fixture from /examples/_fixtures to ensure consistent auth and timeouts.
- Avoid hard-coding credentials or tokens in examples.
- Add unit tests for any embedded snippet that performs network requests.

Special cases:
- Large rollout batches: for multi-page guide rewrites touching > 25 pages, start with an internal-only canary (login required) before public canary.
- External dependency changes: if the change updates SDK packaging or telemetry JS, require SRE signoff and a full production-rollout smoke test.

Operational runbook (short):
- Detect: alert on page error rate or client JS exception surge for canary cohort.
- Triage: confirm whether anomalies are isolated to canary or present in baseline.
- Mitigate: rollback canary; if rollback fails, route all traffic to maintenance page and notify customers.
- Restore: validate staging and re-run smoke tests before re-deploying.

Metrics and KPIs to track for continuous improvement:
- Canary pass rate (percent of canaries that reach 100% without rollback)
- Mean time to rollback (MTTR) for canary failures
- Number of support tickets related to docs changes within 48 hours of release
- Snippet execution failure rate in staging vs production

Appendix: checklists and templates
- PR description template (copy into PR body):
  - Summary of change
  - Pages modified
  - SDKs impacted
  - Smoke tests to run (IDs)
  - Rollback plan
  - Reviewer approvals (list)

- Incident postmortem template: include canary weights, monitored metrics, timeline, root cause, and action items.

Related pages and references:
- docs-site CI/CD release gates (internal)
- SDK snippet runner README in /examples/test-runner/README.md
- Support triage playbook for developer-facing regressions
